recipes.name: Texas Coleslaw
ingredients_raw: 1 medium head green cabbage, rinsed and very thinly sliced

steps.text: Whisk together mayonnaise, lime juice, cumin, cayenne, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Add cabbage, carrot, green onions, and radishes and stir until well-combined. Chill at least 1 hour before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Texas Coleslaw
raw_recipe.description: Texas coleslaw with a Southwestern twist! Tangy with lime juice, cayenne and cumin, and bursting with crunchy bits of carrot, green onion and radish.

review.reviewBody: The first time I rated this, I only gave it a 3, but I've got to change it to a 4. We had it the day I made it and it only tasted like coleslaw with taco seasoning in it, but the next day it was a good bit better and then the day after that, it was really good. So, if you know far enough in advance, make it two days before you'll eat it. It has a great flavor then!

I will start by saying I normally like a sweet and creamy coleslaw. But there was something about this recipe that I just wanted to try. Because of all the reviews of it being too spicy I started out with half the amount of cumin and cayenne pepper. Because I had a little more than a cup of mayonnaise and I wanted to use it up, I probably had a little shy of a cup and a half of mayonnaise. After adding all the ingredients it just wasn’t spicy enough for me so I added the reminding half of the spices. Now my Cayenne pepper was over a year old so that might have had something to do with it. I found there was a warmth on my tongue and on my lips but no burning whatsoever. I also wanted more of the lime flavor so I added an additional juice of one lime. But keep in mind I had more than one cup of mayonnaise. I massaged it all in to start the process of brining. And I had it the next day and it was phenomenal!

This was the PERFECT companion to the Texas BBQ brisket we ate today. I changed a couple of things: I used purple/red cabbage instead of green; I only used 1/4 tsp of cayenne (and it was still plenty spicy); and I added about 1/2-1 tsp. of grated turmeric root.

We loved it! I had all the ingredients and used prepackaged coleslaw mix. Instead of the green onion, I substituted a whole white onion, which I chopped in the food processor with 6-8 radishes. Delicious!

Oh my word!!! This was crazy delicious!! I made the dressing exactly how it said. Oh wait, I added probably more lime juice, I squeezed a half of a lime into it and just a small pinch of sugar. It was amazing , the family all liked it but I loved it! The salad I did completely different but it was the dressing that made it a hit! So my salad, I used bagged broccoli slaw, one can of black beans rinsed, one small bag of frozen corn rinsed and thawed and then because I had them at the last minute I threw in halved grape tomatoes. The result was out of this world and I only had it in the fridge for a 1/2 hour before serving it. Thank you Denyse for such an easy and especially delicious salad!!
i cut back on the ccumin to 1/2 added also added 1/4 cup sugar and doubled the lime juice
Overall this is a great recipe. My family preferred Garlic Salt to Cumin and I dropped the cayenne out, but again that is my family preferrence.

YUM! I wanted a quick coleslaw to go with chicken quesedillas - this is it. I doubled the lime juice, used a bit of chopped sweet onion instead of green, and omitted the radishes because I didn't have any. I could eat this as the main course, it's that good!

Mmmm, so good! I am NOT a fan of coleslaw, but this was very good! I altered the recipe just a little because I can't leave well enough alone: I added Cilantro to the cabbage mixture, and to the dressing I added some taco sauce (about 2 T.) and about 1/2 cup sour cream. I didn't have radishes, so I omitted that. I will be making this again!!

Awesome coleslaw if you don't like traditional slaw that is too sweet. It definitely has a kick..more like a punch.. so if you don't want to feel the after burn in your mouth try 1/2 tsp of cayenne, instead. Absolutely loved the cumin and that's what makes this recipe. I substituted sour cream and greek yogurt for the mayo. I don't like mayo and next time will probably just sub the yogurt but because I had sour cream I needed to use up I included that. I will use this again in the summer when we start to BBQ again. Yummy and thanks for posting!
I love this coleslaw! I too reduced the cayenne and cumin by half, but it was perfect. I can't wait to make this again!
This is spicy! However, I found it went great with some cooler items. I served it with pinto beans, turkey burgers.. any recipes that could take the bold flavors this Texas Coleslaw brought!

As the three stars indicate, this was simply ok. Although we like southwestern foods in general, I'm not sure we liked the cumin, cayenne, and lime juice mixture on slaw in particular. Husband LOVES hot, spicy foods but said that somehow the cayenne in this dish was "distracting".

5.9.18 This was OK, would probably cut back on the cumin a bit if I made again, which I probably won't. This didn't WOW me, and I wasn't crazy about the way it looked either (that dark dressing). Maybe I'm just too much of a fan for traditional coleslaw.
Tasty but I had to add Worcester and more spice
Way too hot for us!
Modified for large group. It was really good and the flavors blended well. When increasing for large group be careful when increasing the cayenne and cumin since both can overpower the dish.

Yummy! I did follow the recommendation to cut the cayenne. I cut it to 1/2 teaspoon and it was still a bit spicy and we love hot food. Next time I will only use 1/4 teaspoon. I think I will add cilantro next time too.
Loved this change of pace coleslaw but I would cut back on the spice a little, just a bit too much heat for me.
Used this with beer battered fish from the frozen aisle on a white corn tortilla. Mighty tasty! Much better I think than fish tacos with just cabbage and the white sauce normally used.
